A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the GMT/VisionTrack work, and their supplied text, equations, figures and tables are readable. However, v2 repeatedly references Appendix B–E for implementation details and additional experiments, while its supplied PDF ends at the references without that appendix. v1 contains no appendix either. The main texts support comparison, but the referenced supplementary material cannot be assessed.

before.justification: v1 reports original GMT results on six datasets, VisionTrack scene-level and single-camera results, parameter ablations, and a memory-bank case study.

after.justification: v2 reports GMT benchmark results in Table 2, feature and global-trajectory ablations in Tables 3–4, and efficiency and convergence measurements in Table 5 and Figure 6.

M1.justification: v2 replaces v1's appearance-plus-box/time/camera feature fusion with metric-supervised visual alignment and relative-neighbor spatial encoding, including distance filtering. It adds shared trajectory-ID embeddings and averages target similarities for trajectory matching, whereas v1 sums them. Training objectives are also revised. The transformer, Hungarian matching and memory-bank framework remains recognizable.

E1.justification: The six evaluation datasets and pedestrian-tracking coverage remain, including VisionTrack's 15 scenes, 116K frames and 1176K boxes. The newly stated 88 sequences do not establish dataset expansion. However, v1 explicitly uses CrowdHuman pretraining, while v2 does not identify equivalent pretraining data; its missing appendix prevents determining whether training-data coverage changed.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparison changes substantially: v1's OSNet and Strong rows are absent from v2 Table 2, which adds CT and two MvMHAT++ variants. Original MvMHAT remains as MvMHATprev, alongside AGW and CrossMOT. The new variants have no WILDTRACK results. Table 4 additionally evaluates MOTR, MOTRv2 and GTR.

E3.justification: Reported training changes from 45,000 detector-pretraining iterations plus 18,000 joint-training iterations to two 10,000-iteration stages. Batch sizes change from 32/18 to 8, learning rates from 0.0001/0.00005 to 0.0005, and the detection threshold from 0.52 to 0.525. v2 also introduces an independent-view Local control and extends single-view metric evaluation across all six benchmarks.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted tests of visual-alignment supervision, relative-position encoding, its loss and distance filtering (Table 3), plus global-versus-local tracking controls (Table 4), comparative failure examples and convergence analysis. v1 instead provides feature-dimension, attention-head/layer and window-size sweeps and a memory-recovery example. Whether those earlier analyses survive in v2's referenced appendix cannot be checked.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. v2's new convergence curves do not include uncertainty bands or statistical variability reporting.

E6.justification: Many results change or are newly reported. GMT's VisionTrack CVMA/CVIDF1 changes from 76.0/81.4 in v1 Table III to 75.2/81.3 in v2 Table 2; WILDTRACK changes from 61.0/60.0 to 61.7/72.0. v2 adds extensive single-view, ablation and efficiency results. These are revised results under changed methods and settings, not controlled version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 introduces an affine-alignment assumption for cross-view target configurations and formally defines a neighboring-target representation and size-dependent distance cutoff in Equations 2–3. These are localized mathematical additions beyond v1's normalized box/time/camera representation. Neither version presents theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Both retain global tracking and VisionTrack as central contributions. However, v2 makes cross-view feature consistency, trajectory-centric encoding and direct trajectory-target association its defining technical contributions, replacing v1's emphasis on generic appearance/spatio-temporal fusion and lost-trajectory recovery. The abstract and introduction consequently present a substantially revised account of the method's novelty.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of cross-view feature discrepancies, geometric consistency, interference from neighbors outside overlapping views, and the benefits of global trajectories and faster convergence. v1 instead discusses moving cameras weakening spatial cues, excessive temporal windows, severe occlusion failures and backbone runtime limitations. Those specific caveats are not present in the supplied v2 text; their possible appendix placement is unresolved.

D1.justification: Implementation documentation changes substantially. v2 specifies two-layer feature MLPs, new loss weights and L40/A6000 training/inference hardware, and promises future code and dataset release. v1 explicitly supplies image augmentation, feature dimensions, window and memory lengths, and matching thresholds that are not specified in the supplied v2. Missing appendix details limit reproduction of the revised model.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises research positioning and citations, adding MvMHAT++, MOTR/MOTRv2, non-Markovian global tracking and newer alignment work. v1 presents global graph methods as robust but computationally expensive; v2 describes earlier one-stage methods as surpassed and centers its argument on two-stage methods' underuse of multi-view information. The general object-detection survey is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanation and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work is reorganized, MTMC terminology largely becomes MCMT, and separate qualitative-comparison and efficiency sections replace the earlier organization within experiments. The title, author list and journal-style section structure also change.

P2.justification: The framework and association diagrams are substantially redrawn, and new qualitative-comparison and convergence figures appear. The dataset-distribution graphic is retained with revised styling and placement. Benchmark tables are reorganized into paired-dataset panels combining cross-view and single-view metrics, with different highlighting; new component-ablation and comparative-efficiency tables substantially change the presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful global-versus-local controls, targeted feature ablations and broader comparisons. However, important supporting material is deferred to an absent appendix, and Equation 9 does not explain how the RPCE loss is optimized. Superiority claims also exceed Table 2: DIVOTrack HOTA is 64.5 for GMT versus 64.8 for MvMHATTrans. These benefits and unresolved reproducibility/reporting problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
